## What this package is

**This is a simulated design. It has never been built.** It passes 10 of 13 verifiers of `mechloop` with 118 errors and 142 warnings. A pass means the model is consistent with the checks that exist; it does not mean the machine works. The checks have known limits, quoted here from `AGENT.md` ('Not checked'):

> Bolt preload and contact (stiffness is bracketed, not predicted), fatigue, buckling, the
> thermal behaviour of a part while it prints (warping is a rule of thumb only), belt tooth load and what belt
> tension does to belt stiffness (only the pull on a motor shaft is checked), stall detection in sensorless homing,
> cable paths (only lengths), axial
> retention of bearings, closed kinematic loops, curved insertion paths, cables,
> real manufacturing cost (the estimate is rough) and tolerances a process can hold on a feature. FEA is linear static with idealised
> fixtures and no self-weight; assemblies are bonded, which overstates stiffness.
> Guide moments are estimates. Catalog ratings are typical values.
> 
> Clearance under tolerance: gaps drawn wider than 1.5 mm are not examined (a finding says when a chain scatters more
> than that); the gap is judged along its drawn direction only (an edge sliding past a corner is not); adjustments are
> not credited (the share is as built, before anything is set), except Z homing on the bed. Bent parts: springback
> along a bend and twist are not modelled. Bed support: nut axial stiffness and backlash, block stiffness sideways and
> about the rail, belt synchronisation error, the screws' lead accuracy (0.1 mm per 300 mm unless the part records one) and
> the rail accuracy class are assumed and said so in the metrics; nut seating is a rigid-body contact solution (flexure of
> arms and plate not in it), and whether a nut is gravity-seated is taken from the floating-nut declaration; the
> straightness of the extrusion a rail is screwed to is not catalogued and not included; the silicone bed columns are
> meshed with the catalogue's stand-in rubber (real silicone is softer).
> Sprung beds: `die_spring_dj8x20(installed)` (Century Spring DJ-8X20YCS, 7.6 N/mm, for an M4 screw), `thumb_nut_din466("M4")`
> with `add_thumb_nut(...)`, `print_sheet_pei257()` (mechloop/parts/batch8.py; all three read through search snippets
> only, source level "secondary"). A spring is a tube to every checker: no verifier knows a preload. A bed pushed up by
> springs against nuts is held by its studs while the load on a point stays under that spring's preload; put the
> margin in the design as a `Requirement` (designs/printer_v9.py: `spring_preload`) and leave the springs out of the FEA
> parts, or the tubes are meshed as solid steel.
> Several lead screws on one Z are NOT supported by: the digital twin (it models one Z drive: travel per turn and
> summed motor torque, no tilt between screws); the motion verifier's dynamics (one joint, one effort); a generated
> `[z_tilt]` from geometry (you state z_positions and points); `quad_gantry_level`. Boards with more drivers: `manta_m5p()` (five) and `octopus_v11()` (eight). Integrated lead-screw
> motors: `leadscrew_motor_17e19()` (Tr8x8, one fused part) and `leadscrew_motor_17e19_ab4()` with
> `leadscrew_screw_17e19_ab4(length)` (Tr8x2, body and screw as two parts); neither maker states a thrust rating
> (`axial_load_rating_unknown`).

Counts: 14 A, 150 B, 20 C. Ranking is the generator's judgement (rules and a curated list in `tools/build_package.py`); the numbers in each item are read from the report.

## Needed from the design

Data this package wanted and neither the design file nor the catalogue holds. Nothing was hard-coded in its place.

| What | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| the design file's hash inside report.json (written by `mechloop verify`) | staleness can only be inferred: from part count, mass, BOM and custom-part list, from the md5 quoted in docs/<NAME>.md, and from the previous package's manifest. A design edit that changes none of these (a hole moved) is not detected on a first run |
| fold-back length of each open belt end in its anchor | cut length of the X and Y belts = path length + two anchors; only the path is modelled |
| print settings per printed part (layer height, wall count, infill) | strength results assume solid material; the estimate assumed 1.2 mm walls / 20 % infill |
| steel grade and finish for the laser-cut steel parts | material 'steel' is a generic entry (E 200 GPa, yield 250 MPa); no corrosion protection is specified |
| tightening torque per fastener class | the assembly guide can only say 'snug' |
